mina.name: Mina
mina.bio: A design student who stops by every morning before her first lecture.

lines.text: Morning! Sorry, I am only half awake. Exams soon.
Your café is the only place that smells like a good day.
I am building a portfolio for a design internship.
Would you mind if I sketch your counter lamp one day?

choices.reply: Thank you! I will draw it tonight.

choices.text: Only if I get a copy!
choices.reply: Deal! Two copies, then.

lines.text: I got the internship! I wanted you to be the first to know.
This café helped me through every late night. Here, a little thank-you.

priya.name: Priya
priya.bio: An engineer who needs a good drink after long days at the city grid office.

lines.text: Strong, please. Today the whole grid went blinking at once.
I fix power for a living. Coffee is my own power source.
Funny thing: your EV station is on my commute map.
I have been asked to plan more chargers around the park district.

choices.reply: Then we both win. I will remember that.
Shade, noted. Practical!

lines.text: The new charger plan is approved. Your corner got a mention.
Take this: a small lamp from my old desk. Make the café glow.

okafor.name: Mr. Okafor
okafor.bio: A retired teacher who reads the paper at the same table every week.

lines.text: Tea, if you please. And no rush, I have all the time in the world now.
Forty years of teaching. The quiet suits me.
I kept one piece of chalk from my last classroom.
Every pupil I had learned one thing from it: patience.

choices.text: Patience is what makes a good drink.
choices.reply: Ha! You understand, young one.
A shy girl who now runs a bakery.

lines.text: I donated some of my old books to a reading corner for your shelf.
A café should have something to read besides the menu.

lena.name: Lena
lena.bio: A traveller collecting postcards from every café she visits.

lines.text: Hello! I am collecting a postcard from every café. Yours has a charging station next door, how modern!
What do locals order?
In the mountains I once drank tea brewed on a camp stove. Best cup ever.
Funny, it tasted a bit like yours.

choices.text: I will take that as a compliment.
choices.reply: It is the highest one I know!
Gladly. It had a view you would not believe.

lines.text: I wrote a postcard for you this time. It is from the café that made my trip.
Hang it somewhere sunny.

theo.name: Theo
theo.bio: A student who codes tiny games between classes and lives on desserts.

lines.text: Hi! Something sweet. Debugging is hungry work.
I am making a tiny game about a coffee shop. Totally original, promise.
Can I playtest it on you? Only two minutes.
In my game the barista never sleeps. Relatable?

choices.reply: Yes! Bug reports are paid in cookies.
A nap button. Genius. Adding it now.

lines.text: I put the café in my game credits. You are the "friendly barista".
Here is a pixel poster of the title screen for your wall.

juno.name: Juno
juno.bio: A photographer who comes in the afternoon, when the café catches the best light.

lines.text: Your window at four o'clock is the best light in the city.
A cappuccino, and I will try not to photograph the foam.
I am preparing an exhibition: "People Who Keep Cities Warm".
Baristas, drivers, grid engineers. May I take your portrait?

choices.text: Only if the foam is in it.
choices.reply: The foam stays. It is the star.

choices.text: I am camera shy, but yes.
choices.reply: Shy is perfect. I will be gentle.

lines.text: The exhibition opened and your portrait was the favourite.
I framed a print for the café.

hector.name: Hector
hector.bio: An accountant who counts everything, including the sugar cubes.

lines.text: Espresso, no sugar. I have counted: it saves nine dollars a year.
I do the books for half the shops on this street.
Your café has a fine ledger. Honest. That is rare.
I may have optimised it a little. Free of charge.

choices.reply: I know. But thank you for saying it.

choices.text: Please leave my doodles in it.
choices.reply: They are the best-kept part of the ledger.

lines.text: I have never told anyone: I bake on Sundays.
This clock was my grandmother's. It suits a place that ticks warmly.

kenji.name: Kenji
kenji.bio: A food blogger travelling by train, rating every café he finds.

lines.text: I review cafés for my blog. Do not worry, I only judge the cake. And the cups. And the mood.
Surprise me!
My notes say: "friendly, warm, a little crowded at noon".
Crowded is good. Crowded means loved.

choices.text: Write that I make the best foam.
choices.reply: I will write that you ASKED me to.

choices.text: Tell your readers to come early.
choices.reply: Mean and clever. I like you.

lines.text: The review is live: five stars, one smiley.
And a gift from my travels, a cute lantern for the window.

rosa.name: Rosa
rosa.bio: The baker from the shop next door, who trades recipes for company.

lines.text: Neighbour! I smelled your coffee over my sourdough and had to come.
Latte, please. I will pay in gossip.
My grandmother's brownie recipe has a secret ingredient.
I will only tell someone who does not rush the oven.

choices.reply: Then I trust you. A pinch of sea salt.
Cross your heart. Alright, sea salt!

lines.text: My bakery display case is being replaced. The old one is lovely.
It should sit in a café that cares.

bram.name: Bram
bram.bio: A muralist who paints the walls of the city and keeps drinks warm by talking too much.

lines.text: Forgive the paint! I did the wall behind the station this morning.
Something sweet and something cold, I am melting.
Your café has one wall that is just begging for colour.
No promises. Artists make promises with their hands.

choices.reply: Oh, you will regret nothing.
Calm and colourful. My specialty.

lines.text: Done! A little sunrise over the charging station.
Every café needs a sunrise. This one is yours.

vale.name: Ms. Vale
vale.personality: Elegant critic, hard to please, tips well
vale.bio: The city's most feared food critic. She tips handsomely when she is impressed.

lines.text: I am told this café is "cozy". A dangerous word. Impress me.
A caramel latte, and something worth writing about.
I notice small things. The cup. The saucer. The foam.
Yours were... considered.

choices.text: I care about the small things.
choices.reply: Evidently. Do not stop.
Luck is not what I smell here.

lines.text: My column runs tomorrow. The headline is "Warm Without Trying".
Please accept this chandelier from my last review. It deserves to be seen.

pip.name: Pip
pip.personality: Quiet traveller with a talking-sized cat
pip.bio: A mysterious traveller who arrives at dusk with a very opinionated cat.

lines.text: Tea, please. Warm. My cat insists on milk, and she is rarely wrong.
We just arrived. The city has strange lights.
Where I come from, we have no chargers. We have lanterns.
Your city lights up like a promise.

choices.reply: Perhaps we will. The cat approves.
The one we carried together. It was green.

lines.text: We decided: we stay. At least for the winter.
Keep this lantern burning for travellers. It is easier to come home when it glows.

elias.name: Elias
elias.bio: An inventor of tiny batteries who forgets his coat and his lunch, but never his notebook.

lines.text: Sorry! Oh, the coffee. Right. Is it Tuesday?
I am working on a battery that charges while you drink coffee.
Look: it is the size of a cookie. Do not eat it.
It stores one thing: the energy of a very good idea.

choices.reply: Almost! A minute ago it made your lamp flicker.

choices.text: Keep it away from the cookies.
choices.reply: I learned that the hard way.

lines.text: It works! The first prototype powers one little lamp, forever.
I installed one in your window. No wires. Thank you for the coffee that started it.
